_comment: Pre-existing layer-direction violations recorded 2026-05-22. These are known technical debt. The gate test PASSES if no NEW violations appear beyond this list. The slow-lane cleanup tracker FAILS until this list is empty. 2026-06-12: added spectramr.data k-space readers (bart_dataset, ismrmrd_dataset) + the dataset-EDA module (eda/loader, eda/probes) as physics-SSOT consumers — they MUST import infrastructure/physics (fft2c/NUFFT/gridding/ESPIRiT) per CLAUDE.md pitfall #2 (no reimplemented FFTs); same accepted exception as the 60+ core/ entries above. 2026-07-02: pruned stale data_io entry (evaluation_use_case.py deleted); added 2 checkpoint-IO data_io entries (model_builder, conformal_calibration_strategy) + 6 layer_direction entries from the 2026-06/07 hardening commits (same accepted physics-SSOT/metric shapes). 2026-07-30 (#629): added 2 checkpoint/model-load data_io entries (mrixfields_baselines/generator_loader, pipelines/eval_baselines) - both load a model, not a dataset, so DataPipelineDirector does not apply. Also added 5 layer_direction entries (super_nyquist_fidelity, fastmri_brain_groups, m4raw_source x2, transforms/normalization) - all the SAME accepted physics-SSOT exception: reimplementing fft2c/pseudo-GT locally would violate non-negotiable #2. Pruned 4 stale entries (models/dev_experience/enhanced_cli.py deleted: 2 duplicate layer_direction + 1 data_io; spectra_tta_strategy.py no longer uses torch.fft) and deduplicated layer_direction. Staleness is now its own hard-failing gate. Also pruned 3 more stale entries the new staleness gates caught: cli/app.py's scripts.sim2rank import (now only a docstring :func: reference) and the .item() calls removed from disentangled_strategy/domain_adaptation train_step. 2026-08-04: pruned 5 stale entries (4 layer_direction + 1 raw_torch_fft) for the four duplicate transform modules deleted this day — coil_compression_transform, coil_sensitivity_transform, concomitant_phase_compensation, non_cartesian_simulation. Each was a caller-free second implementation of a live job and three disagreed numerically with it; the debt they recorded is paid by deletion, not by a fix. 2026-08-22: pruned 4 data_io entries that the text oracle recorded from prose, not code (entities_3d nib.load, optional_imports h5py.File, infer.py h5py.File + nib.load) — infer.py's docstring asserts the pipeline layer never calls them and the regex read that sentence as the violation. The scanner is now AST-based, so the list can only shrink. 2026-08-22: training_loop grew 1 -> 6 entries (8 occurrences) WITHOUT any new code -- TARGET_METHODS is now derived from base.py's own per-step call graph instead of being a four-name literal, three of whose names were defined zero times anywhere under strategies/. The real hook _compute_losses_impl (144 definers) had never been audited. Entries now carry a count: identity alone forgives a whole method, which is the NN20 hole where growth inside a baselined entry goes unseen. 2026-08-22 (#1398): layer_direction gained the three OUTER source layers (infrastructure, application, pipelines) as this test was elected sole owner of import direction and the matching emit blocks were deleted from scripts/ci/check_layering.sh. The extension surfaced exactly 2 violations, both function-local at col 8 in hpo_use_case.py -- the shape the deleted greps could never see. infrastructure -> application is a rule NEITHER checker had; it measured 0 violations, so it lands as a pure ratchet with no baselined debt. 2026-08-23 (D12#5): training_loop grew 6 -> 10 entries, again WITHOUT any new code -- the detector gained an implicit-sync visitor for 'if' tests that boolean a tensor ('.any()'/'.all()' and torch.isnan/isinf/isfinite), which no '.item()' spelling makes visible. Exactly 4 sites, recorded one per 'if' rather than one per matching call (the 'isnan().any() or isinf().any()' expression matches four times and is one sync point; counting calls would have inflated the report to 7). Bare-name any()/all() are deliberately NOT matched -- as a bare name they are the Python builtins over a generator, and 3 sites in the audited methods depend on that. Correcting the count above: _compute_losses_impl is defined in 134 files (145 definitions), not '144 definers'. 2026-08-24 (D01#16): renamed the scripts_imports key to nonpackage_imports and widened its scanner from the single hardcoded name 'scripts' to NONPACKAGE_ROOTS (scripts, scratch, runners, tools, tests) -- every repo-root tree absent from pyproject's packages=["src/spectramr"]. It had recorded 0 violations since it was written while 2 real ones sat at cli/app.py:474,487 (col 8, function-local), which break spectramr list-features on every wheel install. Recorded here as one entry (both sites are the same file+import); the relocation of tools/generate_feature_matrix.py and tools/feature_introspection.py into the package is filed as #1492. The scanner skips relative ImportFrom nodes: ast drops the leading dots, so 'from .tools import x' arrives as the bare name 'tools' and the first-segment match condemned a legal in-package import of src/spectramr/tools/. 2026-10-10: infrastructure/checkpointing/codecs/ became the sanctioned checkpoint-IO home; safetensors load_file/safe_open are now detected, and the 3 pre-existing loads are recorded for deletion by the checkpoint-SSOT PRs 3-4. Pruned the stale failure_gallery.py nib.load entry. 2026-10-21 (#3119): the raw_torch_fft scanner parses instead of grepping, so a string, comment or docstring naming torch.fft no longer counts and aliased imports do. Pruned 7 entries whose only match was prose (fourier, tio_physics, pinn_strategy, ssad, cross_contrast_cross_domain_generator, kspace_consistency_tta_loss, spectral_radial_prior_loss); the two files it newly found (cold_mri_kspace_scheduler, meta_varnet) only carried a dead `import torch.fft`, deleted rather than baselined.

training_loop.note: Recorded 2026-07-30. Per-step metric dict materialised inside the step.
unique().tolist() drives a Python loop over contrasts -- a sync AND a host-side loop per step. The worst of the eight; a scatter/index_add keeps it on device.
Three .item()s building a diagnostic f-string. Guarded by a debug condition, so the sync is conditional -- but the guard is evaluated per step and the string is built eagerly.
NaN/Inf fraction for a warning, on a branch already gated by isnan().any() -- itself a sync. Cheapest of the eight to justify: it only fires when the step is already going wrong.
torch.randint(...).item() picks an operator EVERY step. No debug guard, unconditional sync; a host-side RNG would remove it outright.
PINN loss formatted into a debug log line inside the step.

Recorded 2026-08-23 by the D12#5 implicit-sync visitor. 'not torch.isfinite(loss_output.total)' booleans a tensor, so the branch waits on the GPU every step, unconditionally. Its body is also the fabricated zero-grad leaf that guided_sr_strategy's own comment calls out as pitfall #10 -- filed as #1471; the sync is what this entry records.

Recorded 2026-08-23 by the D12#5 implicit-sync visitor. This is the 'isnan().any() or isinf().any()' guard the sibling item() entry already described as 'a branch already gated by isnan().any() -- itself a sync'. It is now detected, not merely mentioned in a note.

Recorded 2026-08-23 by the D12#5 implicit-sync visitor. 'not torch.isfinite(total)' guards a deliberate instability warning. Cheapest of the four to justify -- the expensive half only runs when the step is already going wrong -- but the test itself syncs every step.
Recorded 2026-08-23 by the D12#5 implicit-sync visitor. 'mask_expanded.any()' gates a telemetry-only masked_mse. Unconditional per-step sync for a metric; a torch.where keeps it on device.
